This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 170ca481f0aeec14ca06d74ec3d57c654997e698` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0c863ce938cf7879bed3aa6c97d070b6612387ba` — the merge of head `d6f24785edef951c39479f85405b1d4d55e3379f` into base `170ca481f0aeec14ca06d74ec3d57c654997e698`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 0c863ce938cf7879bed3aa6c97d070b6612387ba && git checkout 0c863ce938cf7879bed3aa6c97d070b6612387ba
```

### ① Derived judgments

- **`buildDefaultPageSchema` output (published, `@object-ui/plugin-detail`): right.** The default page no longer emits `record:highlights` or `record:path`. This is a change of meaning, not a narrowing. This is the maintainer's ruling 「把阶段条和关键字段条去掉，是的」 (2026-11-20 17:16:59Z), recorded in the #35891 claim and quoted in the PR body. The epic's supersession table (#35595 → #35891) agrees.

The host-bar branch and the own-row branch are exclusive, so the host's control mounts once. - **`RecordStageMenu` and `RecordStageMenuProps` on the `@object-ui/plugin-detail` entry: right.** It reads the record context, mounts the row-scoped field-access scope, and asks `useStageChange` the same pressable verdict `record:path` asks (page `canEdit` with the approval lock, readonly or computed, `recordEdit`, the row grant, an open draft). With it on, the move and the asked-for fields go in one `updateVia` with `ifMatch`. A refusal stays in the dialog, and only fields this reader may fill join the form. The client only picks which fields to ask for, and the server stays the validator (objectui#6868). See nit 2 on how the Clause-② line words it.
- **Four `detail.stageMenu*` keys in all 11 `@object-ui/i18n` locales and in `DETAIL_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS`: right.** They are additive.

A kind takes at least one moved package to minor, and plugin-detail (where the meaning moved) and lint are minor. The i18n keys are a non-protocol widening, so patch is right under ruling A.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, in both: right. Exports and optional members are added, nothing is removed or renamed, and nothing an author writes is refused, so no `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker is owed. The member list is accurate in substance, with two wording issues: nit 2 (it names a non-entry hook) and the lint widening it leaves out (named in ①, carried by the changeset).
- `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flags, each answered:**
  - Owner shown twice when a group places `owner_id` (#35941): accepted. This was already the case on `main` for an object declaring no highlights, and is now also the case with highlights declared.
  - `records-forms.master-detail-body-tables` acceptance[0] wording (#35889): accepted. That item is rewritten by its own card.
  - The spec `highlightFields` describe, the Studio help text, the generated `record:details.hideFields` description and the `RECORD_HIGHLIGHTS_MAX` JSDoc (#35943): accepted. They regenerate from `packages/spec`, which would change this PR's face. Until then the published `hideFields` description ("filled with the fields already shown in `record:highlights`") is false. The card carries it.
  - `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/record-page.md` (#35942): accepted, as a skills-lane card.
  - Overlap with #35925 in rule (d) of `validate-semantic-roles.ts`: accepted. The two readings compose. Whichever PR lands second resolves the conflict and keeps both: list members counted, highlights not hidden.
  - #35853, the two-row header in flight on `RecordDetailView.tsx`: accepted. The menu rides `RecordHeaderState.stage`, wherever the status tag lands.
- **`open_questions`:** none in the claim, the PR body or the cards. The coordinator's two added items on #35891 (list every stage and grey the unreachable ones; the plain status field gets the same menu) are implemented as written, and no maintainer objection is on record.
- **SQL push-down:** no finding. The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join. The menu reads the record and object definition the record context already holds. `fieldsNeededAt` judges `requiredWhen` over that row in memory, with no read. The move is one write. The `RecordFieldAccessForRecord` mount asks the per-row `GET /data/{object}/{id}/field-access` projection, which is seeded at first paint and asked again after a write. That is a permission projection the server computes, not a join or an id list.

1. **should-fix:** `BuildPageOptions.highlightFields`, `.statusField` and `.stages` (on `buildDefaultPageSchema`) and `buildDefaultTabs`'s `highlightFields` and `statusField` are published options that are now accepted and never read, while their JSDoc still promises an override. Fix: mark them in the JSDoc as accepted-but-unread, naming #35891, as this file already does for `titleField` (objectui#7287), and add one changeset line saying so. Or file a card to enforce or remove them, and name it in the PR body.
2. **nit:** The Clause-② line and the changeset bullet name "an optional third `options` parameter on `useStageChange`" as a public member. `useStageChange` and the new `StageChangeOptions` are not exported from the `@object-ui/plugin-detail` entry, so this is package-internal. It overstates the surface and does no harm.
3. **nit:** `field-group-shadowed` (d) now judges only title-only groups, yet still runs only on objects that declare `highlightFields`. That condition no longer bears on what the rule checks. The reach was kept on purpose (widening it would add warnings), and the comment says so. A later card may widen it.
